canonical_name: Max-flow min-cut theorem family for finite capacitated networks
literal_source_claim_zh: 网络流的最大值等于最小割容量
literal_source_claim_en: The maximum value of a network flow equals the minimum cut capacity.
source_attribution: L. R. Ford / D. R. Fulkerson, 1956
canonical_statement: For every finite undirected graph with distinct source and sink vertices and a strictly positive real capacity on each graph arc, there are a maximal feasible finite nonnegative weighted collection of non-self-intersecting source-to-sink chains and a minimum disconnecting arc set whose values are equal.
canonical_claim: For every finite undirected graph with distinct source and sink vertices and a strictly positive real capacity on each graph arc, there are a maximal feasible finite nonnegative weighted collection of non-self-intersecting source-to-sink chains and a minimum disconnecting arc set whose values are equal.
domain_and_universes: At arbitrary universes uV and uE: finite ambient vertex and arc types V and E; G : Graph V E; distinct source and sink in G.vertexSet; capacity : E -> NNReal; finite nonnegative chain flows; Finset E disconnecting sets.
quantifiers: every finite ambient vertex type V and arc type E
every undirected Graph V E, source, sink, and NNReal capacity function
hypotheses: source and sink belong to G.vertexSet and are distinct
every graph arc has strictly positive NNReal capacity
conclusion: There exist a feasible flow and disconnecting arc set that respectively maximize and minimize the defined values among all feasible flows and disconnecting sets, and whose values are equal.
excluded_degenerate_cases: source or sink lies outside G.vertexSet
zero capacity on a graph arc
degenerate_case_status: No-path and zero-edge networks are included; zero flow and the empty disconnecting set are the intended witnesses, but this statement phase adds no boundary proof. Parallel arcs, isolated vertices, and inert loops are allowed; historical loop-convention transport remains open on H.
candidate_scope_not_credited: a finite directed network with nonnegative edge capacities, flow conservation at nonterminals, and vertex-partition cuts
equality of suprema and infima when optimal values are not separately encoded as attained
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty vertex or edge types and networks with no source-to-sink path
source equal to sink or terminals outside the graph vertex set
loops, parallel edges, antiparallel edges, disconnected vertices, and circulations
zero capacities versus the paper's strictly positive capacities
natural, rational, real, nonnegative-real, or extended-nonnegative capacity values
empty or repeated chain-flow components and zero component weights
disconnecting edge sets versus vertex-partition cuts and inclusion-minimal cuts
finite graph as data versus finite ambient vertex and edge types
excluded_substitutions: Ford-Fulkerson, Edmonds-Karp, Dinic, or push-relabel correctness alone
the integral-flow theorem or an integer-capacity special case
Menger's theorem, Hall's marriage theorem, Konig's theorem, or linear-programming duality alone
the planar-network special case or shortest-path duality in later sections of the 1956 paper
a fixed finite network computation or solver result
a structure or hypothesis storing an optimal flow and cut
generic graph, summation, or maximum APIs from the intake probe
the catalog's untrusted verified label or the excluded THM-C-0096 record
